svg.text: Later wings: the same verb, deeper ideas
A crystal that breathes (variables and equivalent expressions), the Mirror (inequalities), twin altars (systems)
The breathing crystal (6-7)
left pan: a recipe box 3 × [crystal + 4 gems];
the child builds the right pan, pulls the lever,
and the crystal breathes through sizes 2, 5 and 8
3 crystals + 12 gems
size 2
size 5
size 8

size 2

7 crystals
size 2
size 5
size 8
only the equivalent pan stays level at every size
(7 crystals balance it at size 3 alone: one solution);
Küchemann's 'which is larger, 2n or n + 2?' (6 % right
at 14) is an altar that tips, levels, then tips back
The leaning altar and the Mirror (7)
−2x + 5 > 11: the see-saw stays tipped, left pan down;
take five gems off both: −2x > 6, still left down
the Mirror turns every gem into a balloon and back:
the heavier pan becomes the lighter, the tip flips
(now right down): 2x < −6; share by two: x < −3
the floor lights the answer: every size below −3
(a floaty crystal); the stone at −3 stays dark
because > never counts level
Twin altars and the swap seal (8)
blue + rose = 9 gems, and blue = rose + 3 gems:
no fair move on one altar alone frees either
the swap seal: a blue crystal may be swapped for
what the other altar shows it weighs (rose + 3):
2 rose + 3 = 9, so rose = 3 and blue = 6
the Star Floor:
east: blue's weight,
north: rose's;
stand where both
altars level: (6, 3)
